products.candidate: Suppress a non-productive / NMD-coupled CDKL5 splicing event (poison-exon-type), e.g. the event generating ENST00000977893
products.natural_human_equivalent: Closest human equivalent is not a deletion but favourable X-inactivation: GeneReviews states heterozygous females with favourably skewed XCI may be unaffected or mildly affected — i.e. humans who simply make more wild-type CDKL5 per brain are healthier. No human carrier of a poison-exon-ablating CDKL5 variant found.
products.domain_consequence: n/a — product is the unaltered 960-aa hCDKL5_1 protein (kinase domain 13-297, catalytic Ser135, ATP site 19-27/42 all intact); only transcript routing changes.
products.rescue_evidence: No CDKL5 poison-exon ASO found. Indirect: postnatal restoration of endogenous Cdkl5 to near-WT forebrain levels reversed hyperactivity, anxiety, social, motor and contextual-memory deficits and NMDAR signalling in male mice (working memory not reversed); in heterozygous females early reactivation reversed most phenotypes. Cross-target chemistry/architecture precedent only from SCN1A poison-exon ASOs.
products.why: The product is exactly the unaltered brain isoform and the approach is mutation-agnostic, but no CDKL5 poison exon with meaningful neuronal flux has been described, so this is a discovery project whose feasibility rests on an unquantified NMD-biotype annotation.

findings.claim: Ensembl annotates a nonsense_mediated_decay CDKL5 transcript, ENST00000977893 (2,591 bp), alongside canonical ENST00000623535.
Heterozygous females with favourably skewed X-inactivation may be unaffected or mildly affected; blood skewing does not predict brain.
Up to 19% of cortical cells expressing CDKL5 did not significantly alter behavioural phenotypes in Cdkl5-STOP mice.
Postdevelopmental (P42) restoration of near-WT CDKL5 reversed motor, social, anxiety and contextual-memory deficits; working memory was not rescued.
ASOs can shift aberrant poison-exon inclusion in SCN1A, establishing chemistry and architecture precedent for non-productive-splicing suppression.

No CDKL5-specific poison-exon or non-productive-splicing ASO program was retrievable (searches: CDKL5 poison exon ASO; CDKL5 non-productive splicing TANGO; CDKL5 splice-switching upregulation program).

products.candidate: Suppress constitutive intron retention in CDKL5 pre-mRNA (anchor: retained_intron transcript ENST00000623610)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found for CDKL5 intron-retention modifiers. Same surrogate as above: favourably skewed XCI females, and mosaic males with postzygotic variants, who have mild manifestations — both humans whose benefit comes purely from more wild-type CDKL5.
products.domain_consequence: n/a — unaltered 960-aa protein; no coding change, kinase domain 13-297 and the disordered C-terminal regulatory regions (300-349, 382-566, 646-834, 848-960) preserved.
products.rescue_evidence: No CDKL5 intron-retention rescue found. Only the generic restoration evidence (JCI 143655; Cell Reports Medicine reversal study) showing that raising wild-type CDKL5 postnatally is beneficial.
products.why: Product quality is ideal but the recoverable reservoir is unquantified — an annotated retained_intron transcript of 2.1 kb is weak evidence that a therapeutically useful fraction of neuronal CDKL5 pre-mRNA sits in a rescuable intron-retaining pool.

findings.claim: Ensembl annotates a retained_intron CDKL5 transcript, ENST00000623610 (2,130 bp).
Mosaic (postzygotic) CDKL5 variants can give mild manifestations, including in males.
Early re-activation of endogenous Cdkl5 in heterozygous females reversed most phenotypes except working memory; later re-expression gave limited cognitive benefit.

products.candidate: Redirect isoform choice toward full-length hCDKL5_1 (alternative last exon / 3'-end switch away from hCDKL5_5, or away from exon-17-containing isoforms)
products.natural_human_equivalent: A boy with early-onset seizures carried a variant in an alternative CDKL5 transcript, arguing the non-canonical isoforms are not inert. Conversely, truncating variants in the 170 nt of the brain transcript's last exon that is non-coding in other transcripts gave a range from relatively mild (pharmaco-responsive epilepsy, independent walking) to severe — direct human evidence that C-terminal/3'-end identity matters clinically.
products.domain_consequence: n/a for the intended product (unaltered 960-aa hCDKL5_1). The displaced isoforms differ at residues ~905-960 (UniProt isoform 1, 1030 aa vs isoform 2, 960 aa) and exon 17 adds 41 aa in the disordered C-terminal region — i.e. the switch trades C-terminal regulatory tails, not catalytic domain.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for a CDKL5 isoform-switch ASO (searches: CDKL5 alternative last exon ASO; hCDKL5_5 exon 21 splice switching).
products.why: The target is locatable, but the arithmetic is unfavourable: hCDKL5_5 is testis-restricted in adults and exon-17 isoforms are only ~10% of brain transcripts, so even complete redirection buys a small fraction more full-length protein — well below the ~50%-of-neurons restoration that moved phenotypes in vivo.

findings.claim: hCDKL5_5 was detected only in testis among adult tissues; hCDKL5_1 is the predominant CNS isoform (18 exons, 6.6 kb 3'UTR); 27 human exons total.
Exon-17-containing transcripts are ~10% of whole-brain CDKL5 transcripts; the alternative exon 11 cryptic site <5%.
A mutation in an alternative CDKL5 transcript was reported in a boy with early-onset seizures.
Truncating variants in the brain-transcript-specific 3' region gave a wide severity range, from relatively mild to severe.

products.candidate: Relieve 5'UTR translational repression (structured element / IRES-dependent initiation; CDKL5 TSS cluster 202up/202/205/205down)
products.natural_human_equivalent: A CDD patient carries a C>T at position -189 in the CDKL5 5'UTR that reduced reporter activity ~25%, i.e. a human in whom a modest 5'UTR-driven drop in CDKL5 translation tracks with disease. This is the human proof that this element is rate-limiting; no human with a gain-of-translation 5'UTR variant was found.
products.domain_consequence: n/a — mRNA sequence and abundance unchanged; the protein made is unaltered full-length CDKL5.
products.rescue_evidence: No ASO rescue found. Supporting biology: eIF4B silencing cut CDKL5 protein ~50% in SH-SY5Y cells, showing translation-factor-dependent control of CDKL5 output; no significant uORF start sites were predicted, so a classical uORF-blocking ASO has no documented target.
products.why: A human 5'UTR variant with a ~25% translational effect and a documented IRES/G-quadruplex-rich element make this the best-evidenced non-splicing handle, but the absence of a predicted uORF means the ASO would have to de-repress structure (G-quadruplex pG41, GC>60%, dG -91 to -101 kcal/mol) — a harder, less precedented ASO action, and the fold-change ceiling may be small.

findings.claim: A CDD patient C>T at -189 in the CDKL5 5'UTR decreased reporter FLuc/RLuc ~25%, consistent with impaired cap-independent initiation.

No significant upstream start codons were predicted across CDKL5 5'UTR variants; instead the 5'UTR supports non-canonical/IRES-like initiation with three predicted G-quadruplexes (pG41-43) and GC >60%.
eIF4B silencing reduced CDKL5 protein ~50% in SH-SY5Y cells.
CDKL5 is under translational control in neurons and is locally translated at post-synaptic sites in an activity-dependent manner.

products.candidate: 3'UTR / alternative-polyadenylation stabilisation (6.6 kb hCDKL5_1 3'UTR, miRNA-site masking)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found — no human carrier of a CDKL5 3'UTR variant with a defined expression or clinical effect was retrievable (searches: CDKL5 3'UTR variant phenotype; CDKL5 miRNA regulation neurons).
products.domain_consequence: n/a — coding sequence untouched; only 3'UTR length/occupancy changes, protein is unaltered 960-aa CDKL5.
products.rescue_evidence: None found. Only the observation that the brain isoform's >6.6 kb 3'UTR contains multiple putative miRNA sites and 'may suggest additional, previously unrecognised modes of regulation of CDKL5'.
products.why: The product spec is satisfied and the 6.6 kb 3'UTR is a large target surface, but no single element is shown to be rate-limiting, and masking the gene's own brake is the mechanism least compatible with the bounded upregulation window implied by CDKL5 dosage-sensitivity concerns.

findings.claim: The predominant brain CDKL5 transcript has a 6.6 kb 3'UTR with a number of putative miRNA binding sites already recognised.
Reports of neurobehavioural alterations in patients with duplications containing CDKL5 suggest increased CDKL5 expression might be pathogenic, so dosage-sensitivity must be considered.

products.candidate: Transcriptional upregulation via a natural antisense transcript (antagoNAT) at the CDKL5 locus
products.domain_consequence: n/a — would increase transcription of the normal gene; unaltered protein.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for a NAT-directed ASO. The closest validated locus-level de-repression is epigenetic, not antisense: dCas9-TET1CD at the CDKL5 promoter gave 20.7-fold reactivation of the silenced allele (14.5% of total) in SH-SY5Y, and with VP64 reached >60% expression from the inactive allele with only one apparent off-target gene (CNTNAP2).
products.why: No cis-antisense or repressive regulatory RNA at the human CDKL5 locus was retrievable, so there is currently no ASO target here even though promoter-level de-repression is clearly capable of delivering the desired product.

findings.claim: No CDKL5 natural antisense transcript was found (searches: CDKL5 natural antisense transcript lncRNA locus; CDKL5 antagoNAT upregulation).

dCas9-TET1CD at the CDKL5 promoter gave a 20.7-fold increase from the silenced allele (14.5% of total); with VP64, >60% expression from the inactive allele, verified allele-specifically via exon-16 SNP rs35478150.
Methylation editing at CDKL5 showed no spreading to neighbouring X-linked genes and only one candidate off-target transcript (CNTNAP2).

products.candidate: Reactivate the silenced wild-type allele by targeting XIST / X-inactivation machinery (listed 'poor')
products.natural_human_equivalent: Favourably skewed X-inactivation females who are unaffected or mildly affected are the human proof that expressing the wild-type allele in more neurons is therapeutic. There is no human equivalent of global XIST loss in postnatal neurons, so the safety side has no human anchor.
products.domain_consequence: n/a — unaltered full-length CDKL5 where the wild-type allele is reactivated; in the complementary cell population the reactivated allele is the mutant one, whose product depends on the patient's variant.
products.rescue_evidence: Locus-targeted (not XIST-wide) reactivation works: a dual-effector CRISPR epigenome editor delivered by ICV restored Cdkl5 protein, re-engaged downstream signalling and rescued motor and cognitive deficits in heterozygous Cdkl5 E6del mice, and normalised network activity in patient-derived neural stem cells and cortical organoids (preprint, 2025).
products.why: The biological premise is now validated in a heterozygous female model and in patient cells, but the validated agent is a locus-specific epigenome editor, not an XIST ASO — a genome-scale X de-repression has a far worse specificity profile than the gene-targeted version that already works.

findings.claim: A dual-effector CRISPR epigenome editor (split dCas9, AAV9-compatible) delivered ICV restored Cdkl5 protein and rescued motor and cognitive deficits in heterozygous Cdkl5 E6del mice; patient NSCs and cortical organoids normalised network activity.
Severity in females depends on variant type/position, X-inactivation pattern and postzygotic mosaicism; favourable skewing can yield unaffected or mildly affected carriers.
Global demethylation poses safety concerns particularly in pediatric populations, motivating targeted rather than genome-wide X de-repression.

products.candidate: Stabilise the mutant transcript by blocking NMD/EJC deposition (poor; product is a TRUNCATED protein)
products.natural_human_equivalent: Humans with truncating CDKL5 variants are the equivalent, and position dictates phenotype: truncations in the terminal region may be less severe, p.Arg970Ter in the last exon was reported with late-onset seizures and occurs in a heterozygous female in ExAC, and truncations in the brain-transcript-specific 3' region range from relatively mild to severe. Truncations upstream, i.e. anywhere removing the kinase domain, give full CDD severity.
products.domain_consequence: Depends on PTC position. A PTC before residue ~297 destroys the protein kinase domain (13-297), the ATP-binding site (19-27, 42) and catalytic Ser135 — no catalytic product. A PTC after ~297 keeps the intact kinase domain but deletes disordered regulatory regions (300-349, 382-566, 646-834, 848-960) that carry regulatory phosphosites Ser407/479/720/761 and the isoform-defining 905-960 tail; only the latest truncations (losing ~905-960 / the 1030-aa isoform tail) have a mild human precedent.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for NMD-blocking ASOs in CDKL5 (searches: CDKL5 NMD inhibition ASO; CDKL5 PTC readthrough rescue).
products.why: Only the latest C-terminal truncations have any human evidence of mildness, and even those span mild to severe, so stabilising a truncated kinase is variant-specific, unpredictable, and in the kinase-domain-deleting majority has no plausible catalytic product.

findings.claim: CDKL5 protein kinase domain spans residues 13-297, ATP binding 19-27 and 42, catalytic Ser135; disordered regions 300-349, 382-566, 646-834, 848-960; isoforms of 1030 and 960 aa differ at 905-960.
Truncating variants located within the terminal region of the gene may be less severe; duplications and missense gain-of-function variants give different, often milder manifestations.

p.Arg970Ter in the last exon was associated with late-onset seizure disorder; Arg970Ter occurs in a single heterozygous female in ExAC, and variants in these late exons may not cause a CDKL5 deficiency phenotype.

products.candidate: Exon skipping / multi-exon skipping (not applicable; product would be an internally deleted protein)
products.natural_human_equivalent: No human with an in-frame internal CDKL5 deletion that preserves function was found. The only in-frame-ish natural variation is the cryptic exon-11 splice site removing 51 nt / 17 aa (<5% of brain transcripts) and the 41-aa exon-17 insertion — neither is a disease-rescuing deletion. Human data instead show that kinase-domain-disrupting variants, including missense in 13-297, cause full CDD.
products.domain_consequence: Any skip within exons encoding residues 13-297 removes part of the catalytic kinase fold, the ATP pocket (19-27, 42) or Ser135 — catalytically dead. Skips in the C-terminal half delete disordered regulatory segments and regulatory phosphosites (Ser407/479/720/761), which in humans ranges from mild (post-~905) to severe.
products.why: There is no variant, no shared mutant transcript and no target exon in this lesion, and any internally deleted kinase fails the stated product requirement of the unaltered MANE coding sequence while doing nothing for mosaic silencing.

findings.claim: The design-space enumeration returned no exon-based options: exon_skipping_applies = false, target_exons = [].
Natural alternative CDKL5 coding variation is limited to a 51-nt/17-aa cryptic exon-11 skip (<5% of transcripts) and a 123-nt/41-aa exon-17 insertion (~10%).

products.candidate: Modulate a downstream effector instead of CDKL5 (poor; no change to CDKL5 RNA or protein)
products.natural_human_equivalent: n/a — no CDKL5 product is made. Human-relevant pathway anchor: ganaxolone is in CDD trials including infants 6 months to <2 years, i.e. symptomatic modulation is clinically tractable but not restorative.
products.domain_consequence: n/a — CDKL5 protein unchanged; an altered transcript of a second gene is the product.
products.rescue_evidence: KCC2 activation during postnatal development alleviated long-term deficits in CDKL5-deficient mice, giving a concrete downstream node with in vivo rescue; also cell-type-specific compensation of CDKL5 activity has been mapped in mouse brain.
products.why: It abandons the stated goal of increasing full-length CDKL5 and is symptomatic, but it has the only in-vivo pharmacological rescue among the 'poor' classes and is the rational fallback if no CDKL5 cis handle survives screening.

findings.claim: KCC2 activation during postnatal development alleviates long-term deficits in CDKL5-deficient mice.
A placebo-controlled ganaxolone trial in CDKL5 deficiency patients aged 6 months to <2 years is registered.
CDKL5 activity shows cell-type-specific expression, regulation and compensation in mouse brain.

ranking_rationale: Best products are those yielding unaltered 960-aa CDKL5: (1) poison-exon/non-productive-splicing suppression — ideal product, real NMD-biotype anchor, needs discovery; (2) 5'UTR de-repression — only human variant evidence that the element is rate-limiting; (3) XCI/allele reactivation — now rescued in heterozygous female mice and patient organoids, but gene-targeted editors beat XIST ASOs; then intron retention, NAT, 3'UTR. Isoform switching is too low-flux. Truncated-protein mechanisms rank last.
